messages.subject: Geostatistical model for misaligned data
parts:
Hello,

I am implementing a spatio-temporal model for geostatistical data involving a response variable and two covariates which are spatially misaligned.
One of the covariates is assumed to vary in time only, and the other varies in space only. Plus, there is an additional categorical spatial covariate.

I am simulating the response with measurement error and linear predictor which is the sum of the covariates and an additional space-time residual u which can be drawn from iid, spatially dependent (iid in time) or spatio-temporal (spatially structured component + temporally structured component, no space-time interaction). 
This constitues an extension of the example in chapter 8.1 of the Blangiardo and Cameletti book.

The issue is that, when the residual u term is assumed not to vary in time, the current inla call on simulated data produces unexpected predicted values that look identical in all the time points (731 days) and only differ in space.
However, the fitted values look as expected for the model in which the error term is spatio-temporal, as if the whole temporal variability was expressed by this term.

I can't figure out what I am doing wrong in the data simulation, assuming the model specification is correct.
 
I attach the script which contains a short description of the data and the model, the data simulation, and the inla steps.
 
Thank you for any suggestion.
 
Best,
 
Chiara

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Geostatistical model for misaligned data
parts:
Hi,
from your text description it sounds like you intended to have at
least one spatio-temporal model component x(s,t), but in your code all
the terms are either x(s) spatial spdes or x(t) temporal AR1
processes.
Your inla.spde.make.index and inla.spde.make.A calls however make use
of n.group, which indicates that you really did intend to have some
x(s,t) components, but then you need to do

f(field, model=spde, group=field.group, control.group=list(model="ar1", ...))

and not

f(field, model=spde) + f(field.group, model="ar1")

The second version (which is what you have in your code) makes a
x1(s)+x2(t) model, and the first version (which I think is what you
intended) gives x(s,t).

Finn
